title: Regular and irregular verbs
subtitle: cleaned / broke - broken
summary: Learn the past simple and past participle of regular verbs (-ed) and of the most common irregular verbs.

lesson.heading: Regular verbs
lesson.text: The past simple and the past participle of a regular verb are the same. Both end in **-ed**: clean -> **cleaned**, live -> **lived**, paint -> **painted**, study -> **studied**.

lesson.heading: Where we use the past participle
lesson.text: We use the past participle after **have/has** (present perfect) and after **be** (passive). The word is the same in both.

examples.text: Tina **has lived** in London for ten years.

lesson.heading: Irregular verbs
lesson.text: The past simple and past participle of irregular verbs do *not* end in **-ed**. Sometimes the two forms are the same (make -> made -> made), and sometimes they are different (break -> broke -> broken).

lesson.heading: Same past simple and past participle
Different past simple and past participle
One verb, three sentences
lesson.text: The past simple stands alone. The past participle needs **have/has** or a form of **be** in front of it.
After **have/has** or **was/were** never use the past simple: say *I have broken it*, not ~~I have broke it~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its past simple. For these verbs the past participle is the same word.
Are the past simple and the past participle the same word, or two different words?
I feel good. I ___ very well last night.
We ___ a really good film yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Past simple of see: saw. (The past participle is seen.)

exercises.prompt: It ___ a lot while we were on holiday.
exercises.explanation: rain is a regular verb, so the past simple is rained.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its past participle. For these verbs the past simple is a different word.

exercises.explanation: After was we need the past participle: stolen.

exercises.prompt: The shopping centre was ___ about 20 years ago.
exercises.explanation: After was we need the past participle: built.

exercises.prompt: We played basketball on Sunday. We didn't play very well, but we ___ the game.
Many different languages are ___ in the Philippines.
exercises.explanation: This is a passive sentence, so after are we need the past participle spoken.

exercises.prompt: My brother ___ in the London Marathon last year.
exercises.explanation: run is irregular: the past simple is ran and the past participle is run.

exercises.statement: All the tickets for the concert were sold very quickly.
exercises.explanation: Correct. sell -> sold -> sold, and after were we need the past participle.
